Thanks again for taking time this morning. BrightBridge is planning a mid-contract capacity increase to support an additional 40% peak token demand across our clinical routing workloads starting Jan 1. Legal/procurement asked for three concrete pricing scenarios we can take to budget:

- Scenario 1: One-time top-up (no annualization) — immediate invoice, prorated for remaining term.
- Scenario 2: Annualize the incremental commit to co-term with our existing renewal (blend/discount applied).
- Scenario 3: Credit/escrow approach — staged drawdown with smaller discount and invoice smoothing.

Hi Sara / Tom —

Sorry to jump in late — pulled together the three scenarios Ben outlined plus implementation notes. Summary below (ballpark numbers, will finalize once BrightBridge confirms exact token mix):

Option A — One-time top-up (no annualization)
- Structure: One invoice for the incremental 40% capacity, prorated to remaining contract term (invoice due on approval).
- Pricing: list rate for add-on (no enterprise discount).
- Pros/cons: Fast to implement, minimal contracting, but higher short-term cost; does not affect renewal cadence.

Option B — Annualize incremental commit (co-term with renewal)
- Structure: Convert incremental 40% into a time-bound annual commit that co-terminates with existing contract; customer pays monthly/quarterly; Redwood applies blended discount.
- Pricing: ~12% blended discount vs list when annualized over 12 months (example only).
- Operational notes: Requires amendment to attach quantities + DocuSign signature; finance needs PO referencing "Amendment BRB-2026-11-01". We can amortize invoicing across quarters.

Option C — Escrow / credit pool (staged drawdown)
- Structure: Customer prepays a portion into a credit pool; draws down as usage occurs; Redwood provides smaller discount (~7%) and issues credits for unused amounts at co-term.
- Pricing: smaller effective discount, better cash predictability for Redwood, smoother invoice profile for customer.
- Operational notes: Requires escrow language in amendment; more legal time.

Attachments: price-models.csv with worked examples (token bands, example costs).

Questions for you —
1) Do you want the annualization modeled over 12 or 18 months? (12 is typical; 18 reduces quarterly hit).
2) Does procurement require SOC 2 evidence with the amendment? We can include a link to our SOC 2 report and generate a short compliance addendum.
3) Who is the signer on your side (procurement PO vs Exec signature) — we typically set up amendments to allow either depending on ARR.

If you confirm answers, Ben and I will produce a final redline-ready amendment + DocuSign package within two business days.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop

2) Show an amortized invoice example (monthly or quarterly) for option B so our finance team can model cashflow and PO timing.

Procurement also asked for SOC 2 evidence included with the amendment; the link you provided is fine but please also include a short "security appendix" that references the attestation and any relevant key rotation/KMS notes.
